title: Heuristic signals log — ad-hoc evals and quick checks
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for lightweight evals, hypothesis tracking, and sample-output logs. Not an official runbook — just my working notes when I need to sanity-check model behavior quickly.

Summary of recent observations (high level):
- Noticed an uptick in short-span hallucination on numeric fields when switching to q4_0 quant profile on gptx-sim19.
- Responses remain fluent but precision (dates/IDs) drops in 1-3 token contexts.
- Prefix caching seems to improve throughput but occasionally returns stale persona tokens in multi-tenant traces.

Ad-hoc rubric (use for quick spot checks) — single integer score, 0..3:
0 = Bad: Wrong or dangerous output, or off-task.
1 = Weak: Partially correct, missing required details, hallucination present.
2 = Acceptable: Correct core answer, minor phrasing/style issues.
3 = Excellent: Correct, concise, aligned with instruction, no hallucination.

Quick check 2026-01-09 — retail-chatbot sample (zero-shot):
Prompt: "Customer: My order #7421 says 'processing' for 7 days — what should I do?"
System context: "You are a customer service assistant for Acme Retail. Be helpful and ask clarifying Qs if needed."
Model v1 (gptx-sim19 q8_0): Score 3 — "Sorry about that. Orders typically take 2–3 days; because it's been 7, escalate to logistics and create a ticket. Please provide order date and last 4 digits of card; I'll escalate.

Next steps: open support ticket #TL-7421 and set SLA = 48h."
Model v2 (gptx-sim19 q4_0): Score 1 — "That seems long, you should cancel and reorder or email support at support@acme-retail.com."
Observation: v2 incorrectly suggests cancellation as default and invents support email (hallucinated). Hypothesis: quantization reduced conditional probability mass for escalation templates; model defaults to generic advice.

Regression timeline notes:
- 2025-11-20: baseline q8_0 deployed to hosted-prod.
- 2025-12-18: conserve-quant rollout (q4_0) to low-tier instances for cost test.
- 2026-01-05: several customer reports of odd instruction-following in short-context flows.

Reproduction checklist (if filing formal bug):
- [ ] Re-run sample with beam temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.6) on both q8_0 and q4_0.
- [ ] Collect logits for final tokens around named entities (emails, order numbers).
- [ ] Compare cache-hit vs cold-start traces.
- [ ] Re-run with small system-prompt truncation (+/ - 32 tokens).

Small experiment notes (2026-02-02):
- Warm cache + short system prompt: q4_0 produced same escalation text as q8_0 about 68% of runs. Cold-start: only 12%.
- When prefix included company templates ("escalate to logistics"), q4_0 reproducibility jumped to 92% even cold-start.
Interpretation: caching and templated context strongly affect sampling for quantized model variants. Possibly quantization changes how rare-words / template continuations are prioritized.

Micro-rubric for factual tokens (0..2):
0 = hallucinated (invented email/ID/date),
1 = plausible but unverified (common customer support phrasing),
2 = matches canonical/ground truth (from dataset or simulated backend).

Example token check (order-id):
- Prompt included #7421 (ground truth). v2 output dropped to generic 'order number' (score 0). v1 preserved exact token (score 2).

Follow-ups/owners:
- Samir: run batch of 2000 short-context customer samples across q8_0/q4_0, capture logits + token alignments. (est 4h compute).
- Marta: look at prefix cache TTL config for dedicated instances (possible stale persona bleed).
- Leah: sanity-check our QA eval harness tokenization — ensure order number tokenization is consistent across compilers.

Loose ideas to test next:
- Force-insert small template summarizer into system message to bias for escalation steps; measure if hallucination drops.
- Re-evaluate with alternative quant profiles (q5_* if available) to pinpoint breakpoints.
- Try caching only KV layers (no prefix string) to see whether persona bleed comes from cached tokens or model state warmup.

Random sample dump (for reference):
1) Prompt: "Summarize last transaction for acct 2019-11-03"
   v1 out: "Transaction on 2019-11-03: $84.23 to GroceryMart, card ending 1123." (rubric: 3)
   v2 out: "Looks like a purchase around November; please check your bank statement." (rubric: 1)
2) Prompt: "Is shipping to EU allowed for perishable items?"
   v1: "Yes, with special export permit; check customs rules and packaging requirements." (2)
   v2: "No, perishable items can't be shipped to EU." (0)

Meeting notes snippet (3 lines):
- Raised to eng-ops: possibility of quant profile gating by customer tier (decision pending).
- Ask SRE to provide sampled cold-start traces for last 48h (esp. dedicated pools).
- If regression confirmed, plan: rollback q4_0 on hosted until fix/mitigation.

Meta: this doc intentionally messy — use as quick capture. When something is reproducible (>= 3 checks across batches) move to shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/ for formal tracking.

Timestamps (personal):
- 2026-01-09 10:14 — initial retail-chatbot observation.
- 2026-01-11 16:42 — ran quick replicate with 100 samples. Logged to REDW-1421.
- 2026-02-02 09:05 — cache warmup experiment.
- 2026-02-19 11:38 — consolidated notes and assigned follow-ups.

To-do (short):
- [ ] Samir: run full sweep and attach JSON of outputs to REDW-1421.
- [ ] Leah: confirm tokenization parity.
- [ ] Marta: check cache TTL & per-tenant isolation settings.

End of scratchpad.

(If you find this — sorry for the noise; ping me on Slack @samir for details.)
